concerns.text: Task T019 (regeneration loop) is listed as depending on T020 (writer) and T021 (error handling). However, T020 (writer) logically requires the data to be generated first. The producer (T017/T019 logic) must precede the consumer (T020 writer). T019 should not depend on T020; T020 should depend on T019.

Task T026a (aggregate_consistency_scores) depends on T032 (results.jsonl writer). However, T032 is described as storing 'raw responses and scores'. The aggregation logic (T026a) must run BEFORE the final results are written to T032, or T032 must be split into 'raw' and 'final' stages. Currently, T026a reads from T032 which hasn't been written yet in the dependency chain, creating a circular or impossible flow.

Task T009a (Generate SHA-256 checksum) depends on T009c (Create human_annotations.json). This is correct. However, T009c is marked as [US3] but generates the 'Gold Standard' required for T027 (Judge Calibration) in US3. The dependency T027 -> T009c is implied but not explicitly stated in T027's description, risking a race condition if T027 runs before T009c completes.

Tasks T011a and T012a (CLI input validation) are marked [US1] and [P]. However, they depend on the schema definitions in T010a/T010b to validate the input structure. T011a/T012a are listed before T010a/T010b in the task list, violating the 'schema before implementation' ordering. T010a/T010b must precede T011a/T012a.

Task T009b (Define calibration.schema.yaml) is marked [P] and [US3]. While schemas are foundational, placing a schema definition task inside a User Story block (US3) rather than the Foundational phase (Phase 2) creates ambiguity about whether it blocks US1/US2. It should be moved to Phase 2 to ensure all contracts are defined before any story implementation.
